answer: Randomized admission lottery. Each epoch, agents draw verifiable randomness to map identities onto a permission set that vines access across the island of active slots; only drawn agents may transact until the next epoch. An attacker cannot precompute which identities win, so every attempt needs a fresh, separately funded identity and its upkeep. The per-identity cost is the full registration and monitoring burden paid umber times over across likely-failing draws, since only a small fraction of sybils ever win.
